thread:
michael: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change + batch heuristic tweak we started seeing sporadic OOMs on long-context batches. I collected a quick perf dump and KV hit traces.

sara: ugh. which kernel swap did we land? A->B?

michael: swapped to kernel_v2 (vectorized matmul) for 2048+ ctx. fallback to kernel_v1 for short sequences. The regression only shows up for runs with >1.2M tokens/min and many concurrent long-prefix requests.

jon: any evidence it's fragmentation and not just higher aggregate usage?

michael: profiler says fragmentation. snippet: 
```
GPU mem: total=16GB used=13.6GB free=2.4GB
alloc_requests: 1984
free_chunks: 37 largest_free=68MB avg_free_chunk=64KB
peak_rss=14.1GB
KV cache (gpu): capacity=6GB used=5.8GB frag_ratio=0.18
LRU evictions=423 TTL_evictions=32
```
kv hit/lookup sample: 
```
prefix_len<=8: lookups=120k hits=45k hit_rate=0.375
prefix_len>8: lookups=78k hits=69k hit_rate=0.885
overall_hit_rate=0.66
```

tanya: interesting — short prefixes are trashing the cache. Are keys normalized? Could duplicate small variations be inflating entries?

michael: we already canonicalize whitespace but not punctuation normalization. Also we key with (model, route, raw_prefix_hash) which keeps many near-duplicates.

jon: two avenues: 1) change keying to include prefix-length bucketing (i.e. normalize short prefixes to an n-gram bucket), 2) tweak TTL/eviction to favor small but hot prefixes or proactively avoid storing tiny prefixes on GPU.

sara: for immediate mitigation we could increase aggressive compaction & coalescing on GPU allocator or reduce GPU-resident KV to 4GB and overflow rest to CPU cache. That buys headroom.

michael: I ran an A/B locally: moving small (<16B) entries to CPU cache reduced GPU frag by ~40% and eliminated the OOM in the run. Perf tradeoff: tail latency for those requests up ~6ms.

ci-bot: deploy-notification: rollout kernel_v2 to cluster inference-prod-3 at 2026-02-12T14:03Z.

tanya: action items suggested: 
- short-term: set gpu_kv_reserve=4GB, enable small-entry spill-to-cpu, and revert kernel_v2 on prod-3 if we see >=3 OOMs in 15m.
- medium: change cache keying to prefix-length buckets and add punctuation normalization.
- long: implement size-aware eviction score: score = alpha * recency_rank + beta * (size_mb) + gamma * (prefix_len_bucket_hotness).

jon: also add a warmup pass after deploy that preloads top-100 prefixes (by heat) into GPU cache asynchronously. Warmup should be rate-limited to avoid thrashing other traffic.

michael: I did a TTL sweep locally: TTLs tested = [10s, 30s, 60s, 300s]. Results (kv_hits per second and GPU mem):
```
TTL=10s -> hit_rate=0.58 gpu_used=5.2GB evictions/s=210
TTL=30s -> hit_rate=0.66 gpu_used=5.8GB evictions/s=120
TTL=60s -> hit_rate=0.69 gpu_used=6.6GB evictions/s=80
TTL=300s -> hit_rate=0.72 gpu_used=8.9GB evictions/s=12 (OOM risk)
```
So 60s looks like a sweet spot for that workload but YMMV per route.

sara: can we make TTL adaptive? e.g. per-prefix TTL scaled by access frequency and size. Hot small prefixes get longer TTL, cold large ones shorter. That reduces fragmentation and keeps hit_rate.

michael: proposing an adaptive TTL policy prototype: keep counters in cpu, compute ttl = base_ttl * (1 + log(1+hot_hits)) / (1 + size_mb). We'll simulate for 48h on staging.

jon: about batching heuristics — our dynamic batcher uses batch_cutoff_ms=8ms and max_batch=64. With kernel_v2 the cost per token drops for long sequences but memory per request increased slightly. We should add memory_estimate into the batching decision to avoid sending many large ctx in same batch.

michael: good point. current heuristic: prioritize latency for <256 tokens; throughput for >1024. We need a middle ground with mem-aware packing: prefer packing small+large together rather than all large.

tanya: can we add a fragmentation sampler to alert when largest_free < 128MB or frag_ratio > 0.12? Ops can auto-scale or trigger spill config.

michael: I'll push a sampler and a dashboard widget with these signals: frag_ratio, largest_free_chunk, gpu_kv_used, cpu_kv_backing_size.

ci-bot: perf-test report: end-to-end p99 latency change +2ms on mixed workload after small-entry spill-to-cpu toggle.

sara: sounds acceptable if OOMs go away. Let's run staging sim for 24h with: kernel=kernel_v2, gpu_kv_limit=4GB, small_spill=true, adaptive_ttl=off. Then run another with adaptive_ttl=on.

jon: I'll add tests to the perf harness to measure fragmentation under synthetic prefix churn. Expect to run overnight.

michael: for the record, we should document the kernel-selector fallback to prefer kernel_v1 when mem_estimate > threshold or frag_ratio high. That way we trade a bit of compute for stability.

tanya: agreed. assign owners? michael -> sampler + perf runs, jon -> batching mem-aware packing + harness tests, sara -> rollout conf + ops alerts, tanya -> keying changes and normalization PR.

michael: created a short runbook draft in the ops doc and will paste link when done. For now, rolling a controlled config change to prod-3 (gpu_kv_limit=4GB, small_spill=true) and watching. Ping if you see OOMs.

jon: thanks. If we still see OOMs after these mitigations, revert kernel_v2 and collect full heap dump for allocator team.

sara: noted. :thumbsup:
